title: axi4_crossbar AR 1-cycle bubble hangs GPU reads (R_AR re-samples m_arvalid)
description: axi4_crossbar.sv read engine g_rd_engine (~lines 232-280): R_IDLE latches rsel then registers into R_AR; R_AR drives s_arvalid[gs]=m_arvalid[rsel] combinatorially. GPU compute unit (gpu_compute_unit.sv:227) asserts if_arvalid_o for exactly 1 cycle (drops when warp_busy set). Crossbar enters R_AR one cycle later, re-samples m_arvalid=0, SRAM never sees valid AR, crossbar stuck in R_AR, if_rvalid_i never returns, GPU never retires -> GPS_DONE never asserts. Not caught in Phase 4 (mock slave gave arready=1 same-cycle, crossbar not in path). Write engine g_wr_engine has same structural issue (W_AW re-samples m_awvalid) but latent: CPU D-cache holds awvalid stable per AXI4. Blocks bead 777 (SW coherency test) and likely ov2 (CPU-GPU integration). Test ready: tb/cocotb/soc/test_soc_coherency.py + coherency_fw/gen_coherency_hex.py, target soc_coherency.

title: RTL: CPU D-cache caches MMIO region — peripheral access broken at SoC level
description: M9 periph-loopback test (claude_verilog_test-k12) revealed: rv32i_core u_dcache (write-back, rv32i_core.sv:812) caches ALL dmem addresses with no uncached/device region. CPU firmware MMIO stores to 0x2000_xxxx peripheral ring are absorbed into dirty cache lines and NEVER reach the peripheral; status-register loads return a stale cached value. Proven in sim: DMA AXI-Lite ctrl slave write-valid count = 0 over 200k cycles; CPU spins forever polling DMA STATUS done bit. Blocks ALL CPU-firmware-driven peripheral control: DMA, UART, SPI, timer, IRQ ctrl, AND the future CPU->GPU kernel-launch fast-follow. FIX (architectural): add an uncached MMIO window (>=0x2000_0000 peripheral+debug region) decoded in the CPU dmem path so those accesses bypass the D-cache straight to AXI. Requires architecture decision + RTL. Delegate to chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator.

title: SRAM_SKY130 hard-macro branch not covered by default regression
description:
tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile defaults SRAM_TARGET=freepdk45, and the soc_all target invokes sram_controller without SRAM_TARGET=sky130. So the OpenRAM hard-macro read path in rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv (rd_pend_q pipeline + 2-entry skid buffer handling the macro's 1-cycle registered read latency) is only exercised by a separate manual invocation.

Evidence: Stage-2 sign-off reported soc_all 99/99 AND sky130-branch 11/11 as two distinct runs, not one.

Risk: the SRAM_SKY130 branch can silently bit-rot on future unrelated RTL changes, since nothing in routine regression touches it. This is the branch that carried a P0 data-corruption bug (rvalid asserted one cycle before the macro's negedge-launched dout1 latched) found on 2026-07-24 - exactly the class of defect that must not regress unnoticed.

Fix options: add a soc_all_sky130 target, or make soc_all run the sram_controller suite twice (both SRAM_TARGET values), or add a CI job.
close_reason: Verified: tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile soc_all now runs sram_controller twice (default flat freepdk45 + SRAM_TARGET=sky130 OpenRAM macro branch). Full soc_all re-run: 18 suite invocations, 110/110 tests PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, exit 0. sky130 sram_controller pass = 11/11, confirmed built with +define+SRAM_SKY130 -GMEM_WORDS=1024 and sim/sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8.sv (not a silent flat-array fallback). No ordering/stale-sim_build issue running sram_controller twice back-to-back. Log: /nobackup/soc_all_gh104/soc_all_68m_run1.log. design_state.json history[] + memory/verification/experiences.jsonl updated.

title: GH #104: characterize rv32i_cpu_top + sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 at ss/ff corners (macro timing is nom_tt-only)
description:
Both hard macros used in the Sky130 SoC (rv32i_cpu_top from Stage-1 CPU sign-off, and sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 from the OpenRAM compile) provide only a single characterized Liberty view each: nom_tt_025C_1v80 / TT_1p8V_25C. pnr/sky130/soc/config.json's MACROS entries map that one .lib to every PVT corner via a wildcard ("lib": {"*": [...]}). Confirmed directly from the Stage-2 sign-off run log: analyzing the "nom_ss_100C_1v60" corner literally reads the nom_tt .lib file for both macros' internal timing arcs. Only the sky130_fd_sc_hd standard-cell library genuinely varies by corner in this flow.

Consequence (bidirectional, see constraints/sky130_soc.sdc header and memory/pd/run_state.md for full detail):
- nom_tt results are valid -- the one corner where macro characterization matches the analysis label.
- ss-corner SETUP results that touch either macro boundary are likely OPTIMISTIC (real slow-corner macro delay would be slower than the nom_tt stand-in, so real setup could be worse than reported).
- ss-corner HOLD results that touch either macro boundary are likely PESSIMISTIC (real slow-corner macro delay would be slower, giving more hold margin than reported -- e.g. the residual max_ss hold violation on u_cpu/axi_bready_o, -70.8ps, is plausibly non-existent in real silicon).

This means Stage-2's timing sign-off, as currently constituted, is a TYPICAL-CORNER (nom_tt) sign-off only -- not a validated multi-corner sign-off, despite reporting numbers under ss/ff corner labels.

Fix: characterize both macros at ss/ff corners for real.
- rv32i_cpu_top: re-run the Stage-1 CPU characterization flow at the additional corners (this project's existing flow already supports multi-corner .lib generation for standard PD signoff; the CPU macro was apparently only carried forward with its nom_tt view into the SoC MACROS config).
- sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8: OpenRAM natively supports multi-corner characterization (process_corners/supply_voltages/temperatures config, nominal_corner_only=False) -- our compile used nominal_corner_only=True for speed/risk reasons during the views-first pass. Re-running with full corners would need SPICE-based characterization per corner (not the analytical mode already flagged as broken for power in bead/GH#104 -- see the power-report-garbage finding), likely another multi-hour run with real reboot risk on this host, similar to the check_lvsdrc=True extraction.

Related: this is a SEPARATE issue from claude_verilog_test-0jp (the 4 KLayout DRC violations) -- track independently, though both stem from the same root pattern (views-first/speed-optimized macro compile choices deferring real characterization work).

Not resolved before Stage-2 sign-off; documented and accepted for now per user decision (65 MHz clock relaxation closes nom_tt setup; residual ss-corner setup/hold failures are accepted given the corner-modeling caveat above, not chased with a resizer margin knob).

title: GH #104: sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 has 4 KLayout DRC violations (upstream OpenRAM generator)
description:
Full-deck KLayout DRC (sky130A_mr.drc) on the Stage-2 SoC sign-off GDS (RUN_2026-07-24_09-58-19) found 4 real violations, all inside the OpenRAM-compiled sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 macro's own internal cells. Confirmed via an isolation test (full KLayout deck on the macro's raw standalone GDS, no SoC context): identical violations, identical coordinates -- proving these are baked into the OpenRAM compile itself, not caused by or fixable via SoC-level PDN/floorplan/routing work.

Violations:
- m2.2 (met2 spacing <0.14um) x1, cell ..._wmask_dff, measured 0.055um (~60% short of spec)
- via2.2 (via2 spacing <0.2um) x2, cells macro-top + ..._bank, measured 0.125um (~37.5% short)
- m3.2 (met3 spacing <0.3um) x1, cell ..._bank, measured 0.29um (~3% short, ~1nm, plausibly grid-rounding but still non-conformant)

Root cause: the macro was compiled views-first with check_lvsdrc=False (OpenRAM's own DRC/LVS never ran), a deliberate choice made after the check_lvsdrc=True extraction died to a host reboot at ~7h. Confirmed these are in OpenRAM's generated assembly layer (compiler/modules/bank.py + the generic dff_array factory type used as wmask_dff), not a foundry-drawn primitive -- searched the installed sky130_fd_bd_sram primitive library, zero matches for these cell names.

USER DECISION (2026-07-24): accept + document for now, do not patch the GDS, do not retry OpenRAM config, do not attempt a DRC-clean regenerate at this time. Full record: pnr/sky130/soc/pdn.tcl (header comment) and memory/pd/run_state.md.

Follow-up: a future DRC-clean macro regeneration (options considered: (a) check_lvsdrc=True regen -- high non-completion risk given reboot cadence, and wouldn't fix anything by itself since OpenRAM geometry is deterministic, only reports; (b) OpenRAM config tweak, e.g. different words_per_row/column-mux, that might shift the bank/wmask_dff floorplan to avoid these spots -- speculative, ~190min+ per rebuild attempt; (c) targeted GDS patch of the 4 exact coordinates -- fast but fragile/non-reproducible from config).

Full-chip DRC signoff for GH #104 is NOT complete until this is resolved or explicitly re-accepted at tape-out-readiness review.

title: Sky130 Stage 2: CPU-macro + peripherals SoC, real DRC/LVS (GH #104)
design:
GH #104, part of epic #102 (bead n0i). Stage 2: pnr/sky130/soc/ — CPU as hard macro (Stage-1 native Sky130 views) + flat peripherals, NO GPU, real Magic DRC + KLayout DRC + Netgen LVS. Template = pnr/asap7/soc/ (adapt ASAP7->Sky130, drop GPU, flip DRC/LVS true).

APPROACH (PD-only; no functional RTL change):
- GPU exclusion = TIE-OFF STUB (not RTL surgery). Swap rtl/gpu/gpu_top.sv for a synthesizable stub driving all AXI master + irq outputs idle/0; soc_top.sv UNCHANGED. GPU optimizes away; crossbar keeps idle GPU master ports. Zero RTL re-verification (preserves soc_all 82/82). Drop rtl/gpu/* + gpu_pkg from the sv2v file list, add the tie-off stub.
- CPU = hard macro: blackbox stub at synth (rv32i_cpu_top_stub.sv) + Stage-1 native Sky130 views at P&R (pnr/sky130/cpu/macro/rv32i_cpu_top.{lef,lib,nl.v.gz}). CPU macro = VPWR/VGND PG pins, 3600x1800um.
- SoC SRAM (sram_controller, 4KB) + boot_rom (4KB): keep BEHAVIORAL (flat flops ~32K each -> ~25-30K cells total). 'flat peripherals' per issue; avoids a 2nd SRAM-macro Magic artifact. Note added die area.
- sv2v frontend (soc-synth-needs-sv2v): new make sky130-soc-sv2v target, SV file list = ASAP7 list minus GPU + the tie-off stub; json_header_soc.py workaround for soc_top port stub.

FILES TO CREATE (pnr/sky130/soc/): config.json, constraints/sky130_soc.sdc, pdn.tcl, macro_placement.cfg, gpu_top_tieoff.sv, rv32i_cpu_top_stub.sv, soc_top_ports.v, json_header_soc.py, gen scripts; pnr/Makefile targets sky130-soc-sv2v + librelane-sky130-soc.

KEY CONFIG:
- Clock ~75 MHz (Sky130 CPU ceiling; no GPU governing). Apply set_driving_cell on inputs (Stage-1/CodeRabbit lesson) for honest timing.
- Die: must exceed CPU macro 3600x1800 + flat logic; est ~5000x2400um, util ~40-50%. PD agent to size.
- PDN: sky130 met1-5 grid + CPU macro M4/M5 ring; PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS=".*u_cpu.* VPWR VGND vccd1 vssd1"; PDN_CONNECT_MACROS_TO_GRID=true.
- RUN_MAGIC_DRC=true, RUN_KLAYOUT_DRC=true, RUN_LVS=true.
- CPU macro in MACROS object (Stage-1 lesson) so Magic DRC blackboxes it (avoid flattening macro GDS -> phantom li.3). EXTRA_SPICE_MODELS = CPU macro spice + any SRAM spice for Netgen LVS.
- Portable pdk_dir:: paths (CodeRabbit lesson). GPL/DPL_CELL_PADDING=4 (Stage-1 lesson).

RISKS: (1) CPU-macro Magic DRC artifact (same class as Stage-1 SRAM; KLayout authoritative). (2) Behavioral SoC SRAM/ROM flop area bloats die. (3) LVS needs CPU macro spice/netlist + correct PG. (4) sv2v file-list drift. (5) CPU macro PG (VPWR/VGND) -> SoC PDN connection correctness (floating-domain risk).

GATE: KLayout DRC=0, Netgen LVS=MATCH, Magic DRC (expect macro artifact -> documented, KLayout authoritative), timing met @~75MHz honest (with set_driving_cell), PDN connected (CPU macro powered). Record fmax/power/area + DRC/LVS logs.

EXECUTION: chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator (read PD memories + knowledge.md first). PD-only -> no functional re-verification.

title: apb4_register_bank: range check truncates N_REGS at max bank size (GH #87)
description: CodeRabbit follow-up PR #84, pre-existing latent edge. WORDW'(N_REGS) cast wraps to 0 when N_REGS==2**WORDW exactly -> write/read guards reject every access at max bank size. Latent today: all banks N_REGS<2**WORDW. Phase 6 adds ~6 new peripheral banks that could hit max. FIX: compare addr_word against integer-sized N_REGS first, then slice for indexing (write+read paths). RTL->rtl-design-orchestrator, verify apb4_register_bank unit suite + soc_all.

title: PLL safety: clearing pll_enable (CONTROL[0]) self-bricks the SoC
description: CodeRabbit (PR #88) MAJOR, pre-existing (not introduced by the pll_subsystem refactor; same gating in old pll_axil_regs). pll_enable=CONTROL[0] in pll_apb_regs (clk_i domain, reset default=1). If firmware clears it: pll_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_enable->0 -> PLL held in reset -> pll_locked->0 -> core_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_locked->0 -> resets CPU+soc_bus. pll_apb_regs is NOT reset by core_rst_n (clk_i domain) so pll_enable stays 0 -> permanent deadlock; the APB master that wrote 0 is gone before it can write 1 back. FIX OPTIONS: (a) make CONTROL[0] set-only / non-clearable in SoC integration (firmware can enable, not disable); or (b) gate PLL reconfig so it doesn't drop core_rst_n in a non-recoverable way; or (c) add a startup/watchdog recovery. Functional design change -> own PR + soc_all re-verify. Natural to fold into #4 (3-PLL/CDC) where PLL control is reworked. NOT fixed in the refactor PR #88 (which preserved existing behavior).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #108 — CONTROL[0] non-clearable (WMASK 03F1->03F0)

title: CPU CSR read-mux retiming: restore 1418 MHz after M7 perf counters
description: M7 perf-counter CSRs (mcycle/minstret 64b, mhpmcounter3-5, mcountinhibit) widened the CSR read decode/rdata mux in rv32i_csr_file.sv, regressing ASAP7 CPU setup timing from Run 43 (1418 MHz, WNS +5.97 ps) to WNS -56.16 ps / TNS -173.4 ps at 705 ps (~1313 MHz) in run RUN_2026-06-02_17-49-55. Critical path = wide OR4/OR5/NOR5/NAND5 reduction tree, Path Group PIPELINE, in the CSR address-match -> rdata mux (NOT the 64-bit adder). Hold/DRC/antenna clean. Fix: retime/restructure CSR read decode (balanced one-hot mux tree, pre-decoded csr_addr select, and/or register rdata if pipeline-safe) to restore WNS>=0 at 705 ps. Must preserve test_perf_counters 7/7 + full CPU regression + CSR functional semantics. Execute via rtl-design-orchestrator for RTL; verification-orchestrator for re-verify; physical-design-orchestrator for confirming resynth. Blocks M11.
notes: Attempt 1 (read-mux 2-level restructure, commit 9d8f64a) verified 192/192 but timing-INEFFECTIVE: ASAP7 re-run RUN_2026-06-02_18-52-22 gave WNS -89.4ps/TNS -7646ps/259 endpoints (worse than pre-fix -56/-173). Diagnosis: worst-path depth unchanged (56->58 gates), violations dominated by 2 high-fanout startpoint regs (_53435_ 468 paths, _57540_ 350 paths) = counter/control cone, NOT read mux. Real limiter likely 64b mcycle/minstret increment adders + mcountinhibit/csr_write high-fanout write-wins mux across ~224 counter flops. PD-orchestrator producing concrete fix spec. SoC clock GPU-governed ~571MHz, so reduced standalone fmax is an acceptable fallback.
close_reason: Resolved by relaxing CPU ASAP7 clock to 780 ps. Flat-case M7 RTL (read-mux restructure reverted as ineffective) re-signs-off clean at run RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12: setup WNS +24.01ps/TNS 0, hold +28.14ps/0, slew/cap/antenna 0, 24.38mW, 4058um2 stdcell, achievable ~1323MHz. 1418MHz does not hold with M7 (limiter=836-fanout counter-write-enable cone, not read mux); moot for SoC (GPU-governed ~571MHz, >2x margin). config.json+asap7.sdc at 780ps. Counter-enable RTL restructure left as future option. Docs updated.

This invalidates the Phase 2+3 ASAP7 CPU timing sign-off (Run 43, 1418 MHz / 27.27 mW / 3844 um2). Re-run synthesis + STA on ASAP7 (make librelane-asap7) to confirm WNS>=0 / TNS=0 hold; 64-bit increment adder is the likely new critical path. Watch mcycle carry chain + CSR rdata mux. title: UART/SPI hardening: real-pin tests + framing/overflow IRQ
description: Deferred M4 review findings (non-blocking, loopback-invisible). UART: (1) real async uart_rx_i RX test (non-loopback, drive raw bits at baud) — 2-FF sync added but untested path; (2) STOP-bit framing-error detect + status bit (currently corrupted frame silently queued); (3) TX-empty IRQ fires at reset when irq_tx_empty_en set before first push — doc or add tx_was_nonempty sticky; (4) 1x oversample documented limit — add 16x for external use. SPI: (5) real spi_miso_i pin test (non-loopback); (6) RX FIFO overflow test (push 5 without drain, verify drop); (7) CPHA=0 1-clk early external sample — documented (CLK_DIV>=7), revisit if real slave added. Both: (8) snoop captures wdata[7:0] only — sub-word/byte-lane AXI-Lite writes from non-CPU master (DMA) would push wrong byte. Source: code-reviewer 2026-06-01.
close_reason: Full external-grade hardening: 16x oversample RX + majority vote, STOP framing-error UART_STATUS[6], sticky TX-empty IRQ, WSTRB byte-lane snoop (UART+SPI); +8 new tests. UART 11/11, SPI 13/13, soc_all + Phase1-4 rollup green.

title: M11: Physical design (ASAP7, hierarchical)
description: Full SoC synthesis + P&R + STA on ASAP7 (hierarchical, GPU/CPU macros). phase5_soc.sdc/upf; power-domain validation (PD_CPU/GPU/SRAM/PERIPH). Execute via: physical-design-orchestrator (LibreLane flow owner). Deps: M8/M9. See plan M11.
design: Macro strategy (decided 2026-06-01): peripherals (timer/irq/dma) synthesized FLAT with crossbar+interconnect at SoC top — NOT hardened as macros (too small, <6k gates combined; macro overhead > saving; fixed boundary hurts ring PPA). Hard macros: GPU (~425k gates, done pnr/asap7/gpu/), SRAM (sram_1rw_256x32), optionally CPU+L1 (pnr/asap7/cpu/macro_placement.cfg). SoC synth bottleneck = GPU; removing it from top synth is the real speedup. See bd memory phase-5-soc-pd-macro-strategy-decided-2026.
